t: A tiny 14-pin chip that plugs straight into USB as a gadget.
steps: Buy a ready-made SAM D11 stick from Tindie, or build an open board from the wagiminator or Fab Academy designs.
Install the free Arduino IDE on your computer.
Add the MattairTech board package through the Boards Manager.
Check for a bootloader. A blank chip needs a one-time flash with a CMSIS-DAP probe and the edbg tool.
Pick the Generic D11C14A board in the board menu.
Open the Blink example and press Upload. The LED on your board starts to blink.
Try a USB keyboard example next and watch it type into a text editor.
meta: Wild Open. From $1.58. A few stores.
